changelog: feat: Re-render in R. The chart editor draws in a browser, which is right for working — it is instant and every control responds — but the report figures are the ones R makes, and a PNG exported from the editor next to a PDF from r_plots/ is two renderers, not one chart. The new button saves the editor's settings, then runs viz_pipeline.R over the same result folder with the colours and Top-N that were chosen, writing PNGs into edit_charts/r_png/ — a SEPARATE folder, so the delivered figures in r_plots/ are still there to compare against and a re-render can never destroy them. When it finishes, one button brings all of them down as a single archive under R's own filenames (04_taxonomy_genus.png, not a tab id). The save happens first and unconditionally, because R reads the settings FILE: a palette that only existed in the browser's memory would not reach it and the figures would come back in default colours, looking like the button had not worked. If the save fails, R is not started and it says why rather than rendering against settings the server never received. A failed render shows R's last lines instead of only reporting failure. viz_pipeline.R gained --settings, --plots_dir, --device and --dpi. Every one of its forty figures already went through one save_pdf() helper, so the device is decided in a single place and a PNG is the same figure at the same inch dimensions, rasterised, not a differently-shaped one. Custom colours are applied by shadowing tax_colors() the way tax_glom() is already shadowed — it is the one place every taxonomy figure asks for its fills, so overriding there reaches all of them instead of being patched into twenty call sites that would drift apart. Only what means the same thing in R travels: colours per taxon and Top-N. Font sizes and canvas dimensions belong to the browser renderer and carrying them across would produce a figure that matches neither. Also fixed: a dendrogram writes its leaf names to the right of the tree and nothing reserved room for them, so on an exported figure the names ran off the edge and the group key was drawn over what was left — which is what UPGMA Jaccard came out looking like. They are measured now, and the canvas grows for the dendrogram and the distance heatmap the way it already did for the taxonomic heatmap. Tests: 17 drivers, 552 checks.
